Prealgebra · Lesson 7.1

What Is a Ratio?

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A smoothie owner keeps the flavor steady by using the same mix every time, three mango chunks for every two yogurt scoops. That comparison of two quantities is a ratio, and it holds whether she is making one cup or filling a pitcher.

Problem
Each scoop drops 5 almonds and 3 dried cherries into a bag. A customer orders 4 scoops. How many dried cherries land in the bag?
Show a hint
  • Every scoop is identical, and the cherries from one scoop do not depend on the almonds at all. Just count the cherries one scoop brings, then ask how many scoops there are.
Show the full solution
One scoop drops 33 cherries, and there are 44 scoops, so 4×3=124×3=12. The bag holds 1212​ dried cherries. The almond count never enters the work, since each side of a pairing carries its own steady count.
Problem
At a kite festival the rule is 3 yellow kites for every 5 red ones. One cluster has 9 yellow kites. How many red kites are in the cluster?
Show a hint
  • The phrase for every 3 yellow there are 5 red is a ratio of 3:53:5. The yellow part grew from 33 to 99. How many times bigger is that? That same multiplier has to act on the red part too, or the comparison would change.
  • To go from 33 yellow to 99 yellow you multiply by 33, since 3×3=93×3=9. Apply that same ×3×3 to the 55 reds.
Show the full solution
To go from 33 yellow to 99 yellow you multiply by 33, so the reds triple too, giving 5×3=155×3=15. The cluster has 1515​ red kites. Scaling both parts by the same number leaves the comparison alone, which is why 9:159:15 reduces right back to 3:53:5.
Key idea
A ratio compares two amounts by their relative size. Writing 3:23:2 means for every 33 of the first there are 22 of the second, and that stays true no matter how big the batch grows. The same comparison can be written three ways, 3:23:2 with a colon, "3 to 2" in words, or the fraction 3223​. The colon form is the most common. Order matters, so mango to yogurt is a different comparison than yogurt to mango.
Problem
A garden plants basil and mint in the ratio 4:54:5. One full repeat of the pair uses 4+5=94+5=9 plants, so every valid total is a multiple of 99. What is the only possible total between 30 and 40?
Show a hint
  • One full repeat of the comparison is 44 basil and 55 mint, so each bundle is 4+5=94+5=9 plants. The real total has to be made of whole bundles, so it must be a multiple of 99.
  • List the multiples of 99 and find the one that lands between 3030 and 4040. You have 9,18,27,36,459,18,27,36,45. Which single one fits?
Show the full solution
Each full repeat of 4:54:5 is 4+5=94+5=9 plants, and the multiples of 99 are 9,18,27,36,459,18,27,36,45. Only 3636 sits between 3030 and 4040, so the total is 3636​. That is 44 bundles, 1616 basil and 2020 mint, which still compares as 4:54:5.
Key idea
A ratio fits many different totals. If the comparison is a:ba:b, the real counts could be aa and bb, or twice that, or any matched scale-up. A ratio alone never says how many things there are in all. What it does fix is the size of one group, a+ba+b, so every possible total is a multiple of that. To turn a ratio into actual amounts you need one more fact, the total or one of the two quantities.
Problem
A board game ships tokens in the ratio 18:2418:24. Reduce it to lowest terms. Write your answer as a:b.
Show a hint
  • List the factors that 1818 and 2424 share. Both are even, so 22 works, and both are divisible by 33, so 66 divides each. Is there anything bigger than 66 that divides both?
  • The greatest common factor is 66. Divide each part by 66: 18÷618÷6 gives the new first number and 24÷624÷6 gives the new second number. Then check the two results share no common factor larger than 11.
Show the full solution
The greatest common factor of 1818 and 2424 is 66. Divide each part by it, 18÷6=318÷6=3 and 24÷6=424÷6=4, so the simplest form is 3:43:4​. Since 33 and 44 share no factor larger than 11, nothing can shrink it further. That is exactly what simplest form means.
Problem
A school library returned books on time to late in the ratio 45:7545:75. Reduce to simplest form. Write as a:b.
Show a hint
  • Simplifying a ratio works the same way as simplifying a fraction. You want the greatest common factor of 4545 and 7575, the biggest number that divides both cleanly. Both end in a 55 or a 00, so 55 divides each, but check whether something larger does too.
  • Both numbers are multiples of 1515, since 45=3×1545=3×15 and 75=5×1575=5×15. Divide each part of the ratio by 1515, then check that the two results have no common factor left bigger than 11.
Show the full solution
Break each part apart, 45=3×3×545=3×3×5 and 75=3×5×575=3×5×5. They share one 33 and one 55, so the greatest common factor is 1515. Dividing gives 45÷15=345÷15=3 and 75÷15=575÷15=5, so the ratio is 3:53:5​. Stopping at the easy 55 would leave 9:159:15, which still reduces, so always take the greatest common factor.
Problem
A cooling fluid should compare water to coolant as 2:32:3. Six ratios were recorded: 4:64:6, 8:108:10, 6:96:9, 9:129:12, 10:1510:15, 14:2114:21. How many are equivalent to 2:32:3?
Show a hint
  • Test each ratio by dividing both numbers by their greatest common factor, the same move you used to reduce a fraction to lowest terms. Then see whether what is left is 2:32:3.
  • Try 4:64:6. Both numbers divide by 22, giving 2:32:3, so that one matches. Now do the same simplifying step to 8:108:10 and notice it becomes 4:54:5, which is not 2:32:3. Work through all six and keep a running count of the ones that land on 2:32:3.
Show the full solution
Reduce each one and compare with 2:32:3. 4:64:6 divides by 22 to give 2:32:3, a match. 8:108:10 divides by 22 to give 4:54:5, no. 6:96:9 divides by 33 to give 2:32:3, a match. 9:129:12 divides by 33 to give 3:43:4, no. 10:1510:15 divides by 55 to give 2:32:3, a match. 14:2114:21 divides by 77 to give 2:32:3, a match. That is 44​ matching ratios. Two ratios are equivalent exactly when they reduce to the same simplest form.
Problem
A trail map records two legs as 0.75 km0.75km and 1.25 km1.25km. Write 0.75:1.250.75:1.25 as a whole-number ratio in lowest terms, in the form a:b.
Show a hint
  • The decimals reach the hundredths place, so multiply both parts by 100100. That turns 0.750.75 into 7575 and 1.251.25 into 125125, giving the whole-number ratio 75:12575:125. Stretching both legs by the same factor of 100100 keeps the comparison identical, the same way 7512512575​ and 0.751.251.250.75​ are equal fractions.
  • Now reduce 75:12575:125 the way you reduced fractions in Chapter 4. The largest number that divides both 7575 and 125125 is 2525. Divide each part by 2525 and see what whole-number ratio is left.
Show the full solution
Multiply both parts by 100100 to clear the decimals. 0.75:1.25=75:1250.75:1.25=75:125 The greatest common factor of 7575 and 125125 is 2525, so divide each part by it. 75:125=3:575:125=3:5 The two legs compare as 3:53:5​. Scaling both parts by the same number never changes the comparison, so clearing decimals first is always safe.
Problem
A bakery uses 2332​ cup almond flour and 4994​ cup tapioca starch. Write the ratio in lowest terms as a:b.
Show a hint
  • Both fractions sit over a denominator that divides into 99. Multiply each part of the ratio by 99. Multiplying both parts by the same number gives an equivalent ratio, the same way 6446​ and 3223​ name the same fraction.
  • After scaling you get 6:46:4. Now finish like you would simplify a fraction. Divide both parts by the largest number that goes into each.
Show the full solution
Multiply both parts by 99 to clear the fractions. 23×9=649×9=432​×9=694​×9=4 That makes the ratio 6:46:4, and dividing both parts by 22 leaves 3:23:2​. Clear the fractions first, then reduce. Trying to reduce 23:4932​:94​ as it stands is much harder to see.
Key idea
Equivalent ratios and simplest form. A ratio scales like a fraction. Multiply both parts of a:ba:b by the same number and you get an equivalent ratio, the same comparison in bigger numbers, like 3443​ and 6886​. Divide both parts by a shared factor to shrink it. Dividing by the greatest common factor gives simplest form, where the two parts share no common factor larger than 11. If a ratio has fractions, multiply every part by a common denominator first. If it has decimals, multiply by a power of ten. Then reduce.
Fun fact
A screen\'s aspect ratio is width to height: 16:916:9 for modern TVs, 4:34:3 for older monitors. Scaling 4:34:3 to 16:1216:12 shows 16:916:9 is shorter and wider. One ratio covers every screen size.

So far a ratio has fixed only the relative sizes, never the totals. To get real amounts, read a ratio as a count of equal parts, aa parts of one thing and bb parts of the other, every part the same size. Once you know what a single part is worth, every quantity in the problem follows by multiplication.

Problem
A bag holds 56 pieces of dried fruit mixed as raisins to pumpkin seeds in the ratio 5:35:3. How many pumpkin seeds are in the bag?
Show a hint
  • The ratio 5:35:3 means the bag is built from 55 equal parts of raisins and 33 equal parts of seeds. Add those up to see how many equal parts make the whole bag.
  • There are 5+3=85+3=8 equal parts in all, and they must total 5656 pieces. So one part is 56÷856÷8. The seeds are the 33 parts, so multiply that one part value by 33.
Show the full solution
The ratio 5:35:3 makes 5+3=85+3=8 equal parts, so one part is 56÷8=756÷8=7 pieces. The seeds are 33 parts, which is 3×7=213×7=21. The bag holds 2121​ pumpkin seeds. Check it with the raisins, 5×7=355×7=35, and 35+21=5635+21=56. Find what one part is worth and every amount follows.
Key idea
The parts method. Read a:ba:b as a+ba+b equal parts. If you know the total, divide it by a+ba+b to find what one part is worth, then give aa of those parts to one side and bb to the other. If instead you know one quantity, divide it by its part count to find one part, then multiply by the other part count.
Problem
A box of 84 stickers is split between two friends in the ratio 5:75:7, bigger share to the friend who paid more. How many stickers are in the smaller share?
Show a hint
  • Add the two numbers in the ratio to find how many equal parts the box is divided into. Then figure out how many stickers sit in a single part.
  • One part is 84÷12=784÷12=7 stickers. The smaller share is the 55-part side, so it holds five of those parts.
Show the full solution
The ratio 5:75:7 splits the box into 5+7=125+7=12 equal parts, so one part is 84÷12=784÷12=7 stickers. The smaller share is the 55-part side, which is 5×7=355×7=35​ stickers. The larger share is 7×7=497×7=49, and 35+49=8435+49=84, the whole box.
Problem
A lemonade recipe uses lemon juice to water in the ratio 2:92:9. One batch uses 6 ounces of lemon juice. How many ounces does the whole batch hold?
Show a hint
  • The lemon side of the ratio is 22 parts, and those 22 parts landed on six ounces. What number do you multiply 22 by to get 66? That single number is the multiplier for every part of the ratio.
  • One full repeat of the recipe is 2+9=112+9=11 parts. Multiply those 1111 parts by the multiplier you found, and you have the whole batch in ounces.
Show the full solution
The lemon juice is 22 parts and comes to six ounces, so one part is 6÷2=36÷2=3 ounces. The whole batch is 2+9=112+9=11 parts, which is 11×3=3311×3=33 ounces. The batch holds 3333​ ounces. Knowing just one quantity is enough, because it pins down the value of a part and every other amount follows.
Problem
An aquarium opens with 40 fish, blue to green in 3:23:2. The keeper adds only green fish until the ratio reads 6:56:5. How many green fish must the keeper add?
Show a hint
  • The blue total never moves, it stays at 2424. So your job is to find how much green pairs with 2424 blue when the comparison is 6:56:5, then compare that to the 1616 green already swimming there.
  • In the new comparison 6:56:5, the blue is 66 parts and equals 2424 fish, so one part is 24÷6=424÷6=4. The green is 55 parts. Find the green count, then subtract the 1616 you started with.
Show the full solution
The opening ratio 3:23:2 makes 55 parts, so 40÷5=840÷5=8 fish per part, giving 2424 blue and 1616 green. Only green is added, so blue stays at 2424. In the target 6:56:5, blue is the 66 side, so one part is 24÷6=424÷6=4 and green must reach 5×4=205×4=20. That means adding 20−16=420−16=4​ green fish. The quantity that never changes is what sets the new part size, so anchor everything to the blue.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A vendor packs gift bags with 4 glitter stickers and 6 mini erasers each. She fills 5 bags. How many mini erasers does she use in total?
Show the solution
Each bag holds six mini erasers and she fills five bags, so 5×6=305×6=30. She uses 3030​ mini erasers. The sticker count does not matter here, since the question asks about only one side of the pairing.
Practice
A swim club keeps 2 coaches for every 9 swimmers. This morning 36 swimmers arrived. How many coaches are on deck?
Show the solution
The swimmers went from 99 to 3636, and 36÷9=436÷9=4, so the coaches scale by 44 as well, giving 2×4=82×4=8. There are 88​ coaches on deck. Both parts of a ratio move by the same multiplier, which is why 8:368:36 reduces right back to 2:92:9.
Practice
A flower stand bundles tulips and daffodils in the ratio 5:65:6. One full repeat is 5+6=115+6=11 stems, so every valid total is a multiple of 11. What is the only total between 70 and 80?
Show the solution
Every valid total is a multiple of 1111. Near the range, 11×6=6611×6=66 is too small and 11×8=8811×8=88 is too big, so the total is 11×7=7711×7=77​. That is 77 repeats, meaning 3535 tulips and 4242 daffodils.
Practice
A fabric border repeats wide stripes to narrow stripes in the ratio 9:129:12. Reduce first, then scale up so the wide count reaches 24. How many narrow stripes go with 24 wide ones?
Show the solution
Reduce 9:129:12 by dividing both parts by 33, which gives 3:43:4. To get from 33 wide stripes to 2424 you multiply by 88, so the narrow part becomes 4×8=324×8=32. That is 3232​ narrow stripes. You could also scale the original 9:129:12 by 249=83924​=38​, since 12×83=3212×38​=32 too. Reducing first just keeps the numbers friendlier.
Practice
A juice bar restocks mango and guava pods in the ratio 24:3624:36. Simplify to lowest terms. Write your answer as a:b.
Show the solution
The greatest common factor of 2424 and 3636 is 1212. Dividing gives 24÷12=224÷12=2 and 36÷12=336÷12=3, so the simplified ratio is 2:32:3​. The only factor 22 and 33 share is 11, so it is fully reduced.
Practice
A bakery sells sourdough to rye in the ratio 42:5442:54. Simplify to lowest terms. Write your answer as a:b.
Show the solution
Both 4242 and 5454 are divisible by 22 and by 33, so their greatest common factor is 66. Dividing gives 42÷6=742÷6=7 and 54÷6=954÷6=9, so the ratio is 7:97:9​. Now 77 and 99 share no factor larger than 11, so this is lowest terms.
Practice
A smoothie uses 5665​ cup berries and 5995​ cup banana. Clear the fractions and reduce to lowest terms. Write the ratio of berries to banana as a:b.
Show the solution
Both 66 and 99 divide evenly into 1818, so multiply each part by 1818. That gives 56×18=1565​×18=15 and 59×18=1095​×18=10, so the ratio is 15:1015:10. Dividing both by 55 leaves 3:23:2​. Any common multiple of the denominators will clear the fractions, and then you reduce what is left.
Practice
A window glaze uses 1221​ cup fast-drying liquid and 3883​ cup slow-drying liquid. Multiply both by 8, then reduce. Write the ratio in the form a:b.
Show the solution
Multiply both parts by 88. That gives 12×8=421​×8=4 and 38×8=383​×8=3, so the ratio is 4:34:3​. The factors of 44 are 1,2,41,2,4 and the factors of 33 are 1,31,3, so nothing larger than 11 divides both and it is already in lowest terms.
Practice
Two garden rows measure 0.60.6 m and 1.51.5 m. Rewrite 0.6:1.50.6:1.5 as a whole-number ratio in simplest form. Write your answer as a:b.
Show the solution
Multiply both parts of 0.6:1.50.6:1.5 by 1010 to clear the decimals, giving 6:156:15. Both divide by 33, so 6÷3=26÷3=2 and 15÷3=515÷3=5, which is 2:52:5​. Clearing decimals this way is safe because scaling both parts by the same number leaves the comparison alone.
Practice
A soup base uses 2.42.4 cups broth and 0.90.9 cups cream. Multiply by 10 to clear decimals, then reduce. Write the ratio as a:b.
Show the solution
Multiply both parts of 2.4:0.92.4:0.9 by 1010 to clear the decimals, giving 24:924:9. The greatest common factor is 33, so 24÷3=824÷3=8 and 9÷3=39÷3=3, leaving 8:38:3​. That is eight parts broth for every three parts cream.
Practice
A bracelet has 72 beads, copper to jade in the ratio 4:54:5. How many jade beads are on the bracelet?
Show the solution
The ratio 4:54:5 cuts the bracelet into 4+5=94+5=9 equal parts, so one part is 72÷9=872÷9=8 beads. Jade is the five-part color, which is 5×8=405×8=40​ beads. Copper gets 4×8=324×8=32, and 32+40=7232+40=72, the whole bracelet.
Practice
A 90-minute playlist splits jazz to folk in the ratio 7:37:3. The jazz piece is the larger share. How many minutes long is the jazz piece?
Show the solution
The ratio 7:37:3 splits the playlist into 7+3=107+3=10 equal parts, so one part is 90÷10=990÷10=9 minutes. Jazz is seven parts, which is 7×9=637×9=63​ minutes. Folk gets 3×9=273×9=27 minutes, and 63+27=9063+27=90, the full playlist.
Practice
A potting soil blend mixes compost to sand in the ratio 3:83:8. One batch uses 15 kg of compost, where one part equals one kilogram. What is the total mass of the batch?
Show the solution
The compost is the 33 part and it weighs 1515 kilograms, so the multiplier is 15÷3=515÷3=5. One full repeat of the mix is 3+8=113+8=11 kilograms, so the batch is 11×5=5511×5=55​ kilograms. Check by parts, 3×5=153×5=15 kilograms of compost and 8×5=408×5=40 of sand, and 15+40=5515+40=55.
Practice
A reef tank holds 35 fish in the ratio 3:43:4 blue to gold. The keeper adds only blue fish until the count is 1:11:1. How many blue fish must she add?
Show the solution
The ratio 3:43:4 makes 3+4=73+4=7 equal parts, so one part is 35÷7=535÷7=5 fish, giving 1515 blue and 2020 gold. Only blue is added, so gold stays locked at 2020, and 1:11:1 means blue has to climb to 2020 as well. It started at 1515, so she adds 20−15=520−15=5​ blue fish. Anchor to the count that does not move.

Learn it by doing it

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
